left (r1..3, c0) is 2,2,2

Bottom:
Wait! r5, c1..4 is [3,3,3,3] AND r6, c1..4 is [3,3,3,3]! (2 rows!)

Because the inner shape (8) was size 2x2!
Wait, in train 1, the inner shape (7) was size 1x1!
So top/left had 1 layer, bottom/right had 1 layer?
Wait, in train 2, top has 1 layer, left has 1 layer, but bottom has 2 layers, right has 2 layers?
Wait, why does top have 1 layer and bottom have 2?

9, 9, 9

Bottom: r7, c5..7 is 4,4,4 (1 row).
Left: r4..6, c4 is 4,4,4 (1 column).
Right: r4..6, c8 is 4,4,4 (1 column).

Wait, why did train 2 have 2 rows on bottom and 2 columns on right?
Could it be:
Original box expands in each direction by the size of the inner shape?
Wait! In train 2, inner shape size is 2x2.
Why is top only 1 row, left only 1 column?
Wait, look at train 2 top:
r0 is top row of grid! There is no r(-1)! It hit the boundary of the grid?
Wait, r0 is row 0!
Input row 0 is 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0.
Above row 0, it would be row -1!
And left: col 0 is col 0! Left of col 0 would be col -1!
YES! The grid boundary clipped it!
If it expanded by size of inner shape (which is 2):
Top: 2 rows up (r-1, r0). But r-1 is out of bounds, so only r0!
Left: 2 cols left (c-1, c0). But c-1 is out of bounds, so only c0!
Bottom: 2 rows down: r5, r6. Both inside grid!
Right: 2 cols right: c5, c6. Both inside grid!
THAT'S IT! It expands by the thickness/dimensions of the inner square!
Wait, in train 1: inner square is 1x1. Expanded by 1 in each direction!
In train 3: inner square is 1x1. Expanded by 1 in each direction!
In train 2: inner square is 2x2. Expanded by 2 in each direction (clipped by boundaries)!

Wait, what if inner shape is W x H?
In train 2, height = 2, width = 2.
Wait, does it expand by H vertically (up and down) and W horizontally (left and right)?
Let's check if the inner shape is always square:
In train 1: 1x1.
In train 2: 2x2.
In train 3: 1x1.

And what happens to the shape itself?
Outer color = C1, Inner color = C2.
The inner region of the original box becomes C1.
The outer border of the original box becomes C2.
(So within the original box, C1 and C2 swap!)
And outside the original box, in the 4 cardinal directions (orthogonal projections):
Projections of the original box are filled with C1!
Wait, how far does each projection extend?
By H vertically (up and down) and W horizontally (left and right)?
Wait, in train 2:
Original box width = 4, height = 4.
Inner box: width = 2, height = 2.
Top extends by 2 (clipped to 1).
Bottom extends by 2.
Left extends by 2 (clipped to 1).
Right extends by 2.
And the extension only covers the projection of the box (i.e. c from box_c_min to box_c_max, or r from box_r_min to box_r_max)!
The corners are NOT filled (they remain 0)!
Notice: in train 1: corners like (0,0), (0,4) are 0.
Train 2: corners are 0.
Train 3: corners are 0.
And the color of the extensions is C1 (the original outer color)!
